#### **Executive Summary** 

#### **Highlights of international copper market** 

Although Q2 is a traditional peak season for consumption, affected by Euro credit crisis, US Dollars trending strong and market worrying about Chinese copper consumption in future, the copper price suffered sharp decrease from US$8030/t at the beginning of Apr. to US$6,050/t at the beginning of Jun., down by one forth, which is the largest extent the price falling back since the end of 2008. With Euro credit crisis got release and US Dollar re‐weakened, copper price slowly climbed up in turbulence, and rebounded to US$6875/t at the end of Jun. 

The copper stockpile in LME extended the downturn since Mar. 2010; it kept decreasing in Q2, a

nd dropped to 449.4kt at the end of Jun., down by 63kt or 12.3% compared with that at the end of Mar. Seen from the change of LME’s stockpile, there is possibility of human factors; seen from daily change, the growth and decrease are very regular, most of which are less than 2,000t. Meanwhile, the copper stockpile in SHEF increased first and then decreased; it ever rose to 189.4kt at the end of Apr., being the highest level since August, 2002; it fell back in May, and fell to 123.9kt at the end of Jun., down by 34.6% m‐o‐m. #### **Highlights of Chinese copper market** The domestic copper price followed that in international market; it also increased to highest point of a period to 63,100yuan/t, not exceeding 64,180yuan/t at the beginning of 2010, and then it fell back fast, till decreasing to 48,900yuan/t on Jun. 8, down by 22.5% compared with the high point at the beginning of Apr., being the lowest point since Oct. 2009. After the falling, the price rebounded a little, climbing to 54,490yuan/t at the end of Jun. The copper stockpile in SHEF increased first and then decreased; it ever rose to 189.4kt at the end of Apr., being the highest level since August, 2002; it fell back in May, and fell to 123.9kt at the end of Jun., down by 34.6% m‐o‐m. #### **Chinese Copper Prices** ##### **Copper price hits peak and then falls** Although Q2 is a traditional peak season for consumption, affected by Euro credit crisis, US Dollars trending strong and market worrying about Chinese copper consumption in future, the copper price suffered sharp decrease from US$8030/t at the beginning of Apr. to US$6,050/t at the beginning of Jun., down by one forth, which is the largest extent the price falling back since the end of 2008. With Euro credit crisis got release and US Dollar re‐weakened, copper price slowly climbed up in turbulence, and rebounded to US$6875/t at the end of Jun. In Q2, the average price of cash copper and 3‐month copper on the LME was US$7027/t and US$7,060/t, respectively, down by 2.8% and 2.7% compared with that in Q1, up by 50.7% and 51% y‐o‐y. The domestic copper price followed that in international market; it also increased to highest **4** / **28** point of a period to 63,100yuan/t, not exceeding 64,180yuan/t at the beginning of 2010, and then it fell back fast, till decreasing to 48,900yuan/t on Jun. 8, down by 22.5% compared with the high point at the beginning of Apr., being the lowest point since Oct. 2009. After the falling, the price rebounded a little, climbing to 54,490yuan/t at the end of Jun. In Q2, the cash‐month copper and three‐month copper price on SHEF was 56,619yuan/t and 55,975yuan/t, respectively, down by 3.2% and 5.5% compared with that in last quarter, up by 46.1% and 47.5% y‐o‐y. **Table1 Average price of copper on LME and SHFE** ||LME（U

**LME copper stockpile steadily falls back; stockpile in SHEF hits high and then falls** The copper stockpile in LME extended the downturn since Mar. 2010; it kept decreasing in Q2, and dropped to 449.4kt at the end of Jun., down by 63kt or 12.3% compared with that at the end of Mar. Seen from the change of LME’s stockpile, there is possibility of human actions; seen from daily change, the growth and decrease are very regular, most of which are less than 2,000t. Meanwhile, the copper stockpile in SHEF increased first and then decreased; it ever rose to 189.4kt at the end of Apr., being the highest level since August, 2002; it fell back in May, and fell to 123.9kt at the end of Jun., down by 34.6% m‐o‐m. Seen from the comparison of LME’s copper inventory and price tendency, before middle 2009, LME copper price and inventory has high negative association, which means that every time copper price increase or decrease sharply, the stockpile would be reduced or increased. However, since Jun. 2009, this kind of relation was damaged, which shows currently the market concerns more on future demand than fundamentals; the global economy, financial market and other macroeconomic control information have more and more affect

##### **Global demand for refined copper in Q2 surges** The global copper consumption in Q2 saw largely growth to 4,660kt, up by 8.1% compared with that in Q1, up by 6.2% y‐o‐y, which is mainly stimulated by Chinese demand’s fast growth and overseas developed countries’ rebounding consumption. However, at present, Chinese macroeconomic control, Euro credit crisis, USA economy statistics not well and other problems pressed on future copper consumption. It is expected that the global copper consumption in H2 would fall a little compared with that in Q2, but still would be better than H1; the total consumption in 2010 is predicted to be 17,820kt, up by 5.5% y‐o‐y. As to production, growth was seen in Q2 than Q1, but smaller than consumption; the output in Q2 is estimated to be 4,560kt, up by 3.2% compared with Q1. It is forecasted the refined copper output in 2010 would steadily increase to 18,370kt, up by 1.6% y‐o‐y. The supply and demand was almost in balance in H1 because of fast growing consumption and 100kt short supply in Q2. It is expected the whole year would suffer oversupply around 550kt. However, the demand also fell back since some plants conducted maintenance and it is short in supply for the whole market. The shortage was limited compared with 97kt last year. The spot TC/RCs continued to be low, even lower than **7** / **28** US$10 per tonne/1.0 cents per pound. The demand climbed up quickly in China’s market. Some traders deliberately started to reserve concentrate for good price, which accelerates shortage conditions. Supply and demand of global copper concentrate market kept balance in Q2, but spot market was in surplus, zero TC/RCs transaction even occurred on the market. On the one hand, traders decreased amount of supply to create tense atmosphere, on the other hand, low TC/RCs motivated smelters reduce spot amount, partial of smelters even decreased output. Transaction on spot market was thin in Q2 and large amount of concentrate level was not good. TC/RCs will be 40usd/4.0cent after the negotiation between Japanese smelters and internati

Meanwhile, spring ploughing promoted domestic consumption for chemical fertilizer, which also stimulated another upturn of domestic sulfuric acid price. However, with the prosperous season of domestic chemical fertilizer consumption coming in later Q1 and earlier Q2, special tax was collected on chemical fertilizer export, which held back the export demand for chemical fertilizer; the domestic over supply deteriorated, and then domestic price of sulfuric acid fell in Q2. The average price of sulfuric acid in Q2 2010 was338yuan/t, down by 17.2% compared with 408yuan/t in Q1. #### **Chinese Copper Material Supply** #### **Mining expansion projects** By the end of 2009, Chinese copper concentrate (copper content) production capacity was about 1.2mlnt/y. Chinese mining expansion projects since this year are as following: **Daye Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd** ’s Tonglvshan Copper Mine’s expansion project was kicked off in June, 2010. It can add 8,000t/y of mined copper and prolong mine’s service life for 17 years. **Xinxin Mining Co., Ltd** ’s Huangshan Cu‐Ni Mine’s 4,000t/d project was kicked off in June, 2010. The mine locates in Hami City, Xinjiang with 84mlnt of Cu‐Ni ore reserves, including 380kt of nickel content, 220kt of copper content and 32kt of cobalt content. The project with total investment of 1bln yuan will be commissioned by the end of September, 2011. **Jiangxi Copper** ’s Dexing Copper Mine has finished 7,500t/d expansion project by the end of June. Currently Dexing Copper Mine has mining capacity of 107.5kt/d. The 7,500t/d expansion project was invested in 360mln yuan and took 10 months to be commiss

ioned. The total project with 130kt/d capacity is expected to be finished completely in 2012 on schedule. Overall investment will reach 2.7bln yuan. After the whole project being commissioned, its mining capacity will grow to 130kt/d from current 100kt. Outputs newly added will include 41kt copper‐in‐concentrate, 61kg gold and 25t silver. 

**Chengmenshan Copper Mine** ’s stage 2 was kicked off in December, 2009. The stage 2 with investment of 500mln yuan will be constructed for 2 years, and it can process 7000t/d of ores and produce 14.8kt/y of copper. 

**9** / **28** 

**Jiangxi Yinshan Mining Co., Ltd** ’s 5,000t/d project with total investment of 500mln yuan kicked off in January, 2010. 

**Jiangxi Copper** ’s Yongping Copper Mine will finish transformation from underground into open pit project in March, 2010. 

Jiangxi Copper plans to produce 172kt of copper concentrate in 2010. 

**Zinjin Mining Holdings Group Co., Ltd** ’s Zinjinshan Copper Mine will establish two mining plants which can process 10kt/d and 8,000t/d of ores respectively. And it will also establish a 45kt/d grinding system project. Zinjinshan Copper Mine with total investment of 500mln yuan will be commissioned in 2011. 

**Zinjinshan Copper Mine** is located in Shanghang County, Longyan City, Fujian Province. 

**Xinjiang Huajin Copper Co., Ltd** ’s Tuwu Copper Mine kicked off on February 25, 2010. Tuwu Copper Mine with total investment of 2bln yuan planned to be finished by two stages. The first stage is going to be commissioned in 2011 and it is designed to process 5,000t/d of ores. The second stage can process 10kt/d of ores. 

**Tibet Huatailong Mining Co., Ltd** ’s Jiama Copper Polymetallic Mine with total investment of 1.6bln yuan planned to be finished by two stages. The first stage has finished construction at present. It can process 6,000t/d of ores and produce 15ktpy of copper concentrate. 

**Jiama Copper Polymetallic Mine** is located in Mozhugongka County, Tibet. 

Heilongjiang **Duobaoshan Copper‐Molybdenum Mine** launched workshop construction in end‐May. Duobaoshan Mine is invested by Heilongjiang Duobaoshan Copper Co., Ltd. (Duobaoshan Copper) with a total investment of 3.0 bln yuan and planned to be finished by two stages. The first stage is going to be commissioned in 2011. After that it will be capable of processing 25kt ores per day, and producing 117,648 t copper concentrates (25% Cu) and 1,401 t molybdenum concentrates (45% Mo) per year.  When the second stage being commissioned, 50kt ores can be processed per day, and outputs of copper concentrates (25% Cu) and molybdenum concentrates (45%) will reach 233,316t and 3,014 t respectively. 

**Duobaoshan Copper Mine** is located in north of Nenjiang County, Heihe City, Heilongjiang Province. The resources identified are 9.47% Cu for 1.78 mln t of copper metal, 0.016% Mo for 57.4kt of molybdenum, 0.144g/t Au for 60.29t gold and 2.059g/t Ag for 777.08t of silver. 

**Duobaoshan Copper** is established in

January 2006 with registered capital of 600 mln yuan. Its holding shareholder is Zijin Mining Group that owns 51% stock. Other shareholders are Heiongjiang Heilong Mining Co., Ltd. (37%owned), Heilongjiang Dilian Investment Co., Ltd (9% owned) and Harbin Baifu Investment Co., Ltd. (3%). 

#### **Latest Chinese mining projects overseas in 2010:** 

**Zijin Mining Group Co., Ltd** (Zinjin Mining) announced in May, 2010 that it would invest 1.16bln yuan to purchase shares of Platmin with China‐Africa Development Fund (CAD Fund). 

**10** / **28** 

－ Platmin owns 68% shares of Deziwa Cu‐Co Mine and E cailleC Cu‐Co Mine. Deziwa Cu‐Co － Mine owns 1.34mlntpy of copper content reserves and 131kt of cobalt content reserves. E cailleC Cu‐Co Mine is estimated to own 251kt of copper reserves and 13kt of cobalt reserves. According to research study report, the project with total investment of US$466mln can process 4.5mlntpy of ores, and it can produce 80ktpy of copper and 10ktpy of cobalt after it is commissioned. Its service life will be 20 years. 

**Chinalco** invested US$2.2bln into Toromocho Mine project in Peru, it is expected to be become Peru's largest copper mine. Chinalco invested US$860mln to purchase Peru CopperInc. (CUP) and the prospecting right of Toromocho Mine. Chinalco estimated the project will be commissioned in 2012and it can produce 250kt of copper each year. 

**Jinchuan Nonferrous Metals Group Limited** (JNMC) signed an agreement with Kazakhmys in April, 2010 to jointly deplore Aktogay Copper Mine in Kazakhstan. JNMC invested US$120mln in this project and owned 49% shares of the project. It is estimated that the project will produce 100ktpy of copper concentrate content and the service life will be 40 years. 

The project will be commissioned within 5 years at least. 

**Tongling Nonferrous Metals Group Holdings Co., Ltd** (TLYS) announced on May 31 that it spent C$4.27bln to purchase 96.9% shares of Corriente Resources Inc (Corriente) with China Railway Construction Co., Ltd (CRCC). 

Corriente is a Canadian‐based resource development and exploration company specializing in copper and copper‐gold opportunities. It owns 17 mineral rights of copper mine belt in Ecuador. The main capital of Corriente is the mineral rights of Mirador, Mirador Norte, San Carlos and Panantza Copper Mines. Total copper reserves of these four copper mines are 11.58mlnt. After the project is commissioned, it can process 54mlntpy of ores and produce 0.8‐1mlntpy of copper concentrate (contains 0.25‐0.3mlnt of copper content) 

**China Sci‐Tech Holdings Ltd** (China Sci‐Tech) plans to restart copper production at the Lady Annie Copper Mine in Australia in December 2010. 

China Sci‐Tech acquired the mine from Cape Lambert Resources Ltd. earlier this month for A$135 million. 

Lady Annie currently has sufficient reserves and resources for around 4.5 years of operation at 25,000 metric tons of copper per year. 

Separately, the company also announced it has agree

d to buy Canada‐listed Chariot Resources Ltd.’s 70% stake in Peru's Marcona Copper Property and the Mina Justa project for HK$1.8bln (US$232mln). 

Mina Justa's copper resources support annual output of around 100,000 metric tons of copper. 

The project would be commissioned in 2013, China Sci‐Tech said. 

**State Grid Corporation of China** (SGCC) signed an agreement with Quadra Mining to develop 

**11** / **28** 

a large‐scale copper deposit in Chile in March. 

According to the agreement signed with Quadra, SGCC and Quadra will invest US$900mln to establish a new jointly venture company for developing Sierra Gorda project in the north of Chile. 

As a part of the agreement, SGCC will purchase 9.9% shares of Quadra with 1.42 cad (1.48US$). 

Sierra Gorda is located in Atacama Desert in Chile. It owns 989mlnt of ore reserves and its ore average grade contains 0.42% copper content, 0.027% molybdenum content and 0.069g/t gold. It is planned to produce 139ktpy of copper, 7.3ktpy of molybdenum and 36 ounces of gold. And its exploiting time will be 25 years. 

SGCC is the biggest copper consumer in the world. It mainly uses copper in wire and cable. 

**Xiangguang Copper Co., Ltd** (Xiangguang Copper), a copper smelting unit of chicken supplier Shandong Fengxiang Group is planning to acquire 15% stakes of Rocklands Copper Mine. Rocklands Copper Mine belongs to CuDeco. 

The Rocklands Mine, near Cloncurry, Queensland, will have a 10 year exploration time frame and an annual production capacity of 3 million tons. It is expected to generate about $960 million in revenue annually. 

Xiangguang Copper locates in the south of Shifo town, Yanggu County, Shandong Province, it is a large‐scale nonferrous smelter with a annul production of 400,000tons of cathode copper. 

**China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group Co., Ltd** (CNMC) will construct Muliashi Copper Mine. The reserves of Muliashi Copper Mine are estimated to be exploited for 15‐25 years. The project will be commissioned in 2012 and it can produce 60ktpy of copper. 

**The president of Jiangxi Copper Co., Ltd.** (JCCL) Mr. Liyihuang said that JCCL’s Afghan Aynak Copper Mine project would be commissioned in 2013‐14. The project will produce 190ktpy of metal in initial period. Afghan Aynak Copper Mine was developed jointly by China Metallurgical Group Corporation (MCC) and JCCL. MCC and JCCL hold 75% and 25% stakes of Afghan Aynak Copper Mine project. 

#### **Import of raw materials** 

Import of domestic main copper products increased in varying degrees in Q2 2010 except copper concentrate. Import of copper blister, copper semis and copper scrap increased to 91kt, 255kt and 1.05mlnt, up by 10.8%, 18.2% and 7.1% Q‐o‐Q respectively. Import of copper concentrate decreased to 1.61mlnt, down by 6.0% compared with Q1. 

In respect of the first half of 2010, except import of refined copper decreased by 12.2% y‐o‐y, import of other main copper products all increased, especially import of copper blister incre

ased to 173kt, up by 104.7% y‐o‐y. Meanwhile import of copper semis also increased quickly, and import of copper concentrate and copper scrap increased by 7.0% and 16.7% **12** / **28** y‐o‐y. Import of copper semis decreased to 147kt in Q2, down by 6.0% compared with Q1. But import of copper semis in the first half of 2010 increased to 266kt, up by 7.0% y‐o‐y. In terms of the metal content, import of all copper raw materials increased in Q1 2010 except refined copper: net import of refined copper decreased by 232kt in Q2, down by 13.1% y‐o‐y, but net import of copper content in the first half of 2010 increased by 71kt, up by 2.1% y‐o‐y. **Table 4 Import and Export of Copper Raw Materials in 2008‐2010 Unit: kt** |||**2008**|**2009**|**Q1**|**20**

During January to May, import of copper blister was 143kt, up by 115.5% y‐o‐y. Import of copper blister was mainly from Zambia, Chile and Congo. Import of copper blister from Zambia, Chile and Congo was 52kt, 41kt and 22kt during the first five months, up by 379.2%, 43.5% and 32.7% y‐o‐y. Total import of copper blister from the three countries accounted for 80.4% of domestic total amount. Import of copper blister increased dramatically, benefiting from the following factors: firstly, import added value tax of copper blister (content gold) was issued, secondly, CNMC and YCC’s smelting project in Zambia gradually is commissioned. Output of auto and air conditioner increased dramatically, which promoted the growth of domestic copper consumption. Output of power industry was better than our expectation, copper scraps supply was still tense and it supported refined copper consumption. Therefore, we lifted refined copper consumption estimation in 2010 from 6.05mlnt to 6.2mlnt, and the growth rate was also lifted from 8.0% to 10.7%. In respect of main industries, all industries were lifted except architecture. Refined copper consumption estimation in air conditioner industry was lifted from 830kt to 900kt, and the growth rate was changed from 4.9% to 13.8%. The growth rate of refined copper consumption in power industry was changed from 6.9% to 9.2%, transportation was changed from 11.1% to 14.4% and electronic industry was changed from 7.4% to 10.0%. Due to Chinese Govt. began to control real estate in April, it would affect real estate sales after Q2 and it was estimated to affect all aspects, therefore Antaike changed the growth rate estimation in architecture from 17.1% to 15.1%

#### **Market Balance and Price Outlook** 

#### **Supply/demand** 

Output of Chinese copper‐in‐concentrate in Q2 increased dramatically and smelters increased utilization rate of copper scrap. Although import of copper‐in‐concentrate decreased and output of copper blister increased, Chinese copper‐in‐concentrate market was still surplus. Antaike estimates copper‐in‐concentrate supply will be 716kt in Q2, and copper‐in‐concentrate consumption will be 670kt, and the exceeded will be 37kt.

#### **Price Outlook** 

Despite the second quarter being prosperous season of consumption and the actual consumption also saw obvious upturn, the copper price didn’t increase with increasing consumption, but followed more with macro‐economy and capital. China adjusted macro‐economy in Q2, which influenced consumption anticipation and brought pressure on copper price. 

**27** / **28** 

There are many uncertain factors in global economy future and China purchase much copper, which is expected to become the resistance when copper price increases or decreases. It is predicted the copper price will fluctuate in high level and the fluctuation range is e

xpected to be US$6,000‐8,000/t.
